system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran confrontation: Hormuz blockade, economic pressure, and energy shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: The headlines depict an intensifying US–Iran standoff centered on control of the Strait of Hormuz combining naval action, attacks on shipping, and unprecedented economic measures. Military moves (carrier deployments, naval fire), tanker/vessel strikes, and US threats of new economic tactics are disrupting shipping and driving oil-price volatility, while Iran adapts into a ‘survival economy’ and leverages asymmetric tools. Feedbacks between security escalation, market disruption, and domestic political pressure are the dominant dynamic.
system_description.scope: The regional military-diplomatic-economic system focused on the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz: naval deployments and blockades, attacks on commercial vessels, US economic and sanction measures, Iran’s domestic economic adaptations, responses by Gulf states (UAE, Oman, Qatar, Saudi), and downstream impacts on global oil/refining markets, strategic reserves, shipping flows and insurance.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-energy system (international security, cross-border economics, and global oil/commodity markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil and commodities markets (prices, reserves, refiners, majors)
US domestic politics, defense policy and public opinion (carrier politics, presidential statements)
Gulf regional diplomacy and security (UAE, Oman, Qatar, Saudi, Iran proxies/Houthis)
Global shipping, logistics and maritime insurance
evidence_headlines: U.S. to use economic tactics on Iran 'that have never been seen'; Navy works to relieve troubled carrier USS Abraham Lincoln
US fires on ship it says violated Iran blockade
ADNOC vessel attacked in Hormuz as Trump defends extended carrier deployment
Iran Is Defying U.S. Pressure by Becoming a ‘Survival Economy’
Oil rises after US threatens indefinite blockade of Iran; set for weekly gains
Strait of Hormuz shipping grinds to a halt ahead of U.S.

variables.name: Naval presence density
variables.description: Concentration of deployed military naval and air assets operating within the maritime operational area.

variables.name: Blockade pressure level
variables.description: Intensity and effectiveness of measures restricting maritime traffic and commercial passage along key routes.

variables.name: Asymmetric attack rate
variables.description: Rate at which irregular or non-conventional attacks on vessels, platforms, and maritime infrastructure occur.

variables.name: Maritime incident rate
variables.description: Frequency of maritime incidents including strikes, collisions, spills, detentions and suspicious interdictions.

variables.name: Commercial shipping throughput
variables.description: Volume of commercial cargo and tanker transits through the regional sea lanes per unit time.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting extent
variables.description: Proportion of vessels that alter predefined routes to avoid perceived or actual risk areas.

variables.name: Maritime choke-point congestion
variables.description: Degree of queuing, delays and congestion at critical narrow sea passages that constrain throughput.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium index
variables.description: Average uplift in insurance and war-risk premiums applied to maritime cargo and tanker operations in the region.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: Short- to medium-term variability in benchmark crude oil prices as influenced by regional risks and shocks.

variables.name: Global oil supply balance
variables.description: Net balance of global oil supply relative to demand, reflecting spare capacity, exports and disruptions.

variables.name: Strategic reserve level
variables.description: Usable volume and operational integrity of strategic fuel reserves available to mitigate supply shocks.

variables.name: Refinery utilization rate
variables.description: Percentage share of refining capacity actively operating and producing refined fuels in relevant markets.

variables.name: Fuel retail price level
variables.description: Average consumer price level for refined transport fuels in affected markets.

variables.name: Domestic economic resilience
variables.description: Ability of an economy to maintain essential production, distribution and consumption under external economic pressure.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure intensity
variables.description: Breadth and strictness of economic restrictive measures applied to target trade, finance and critical sectors.

variables.name: Diplomatic escalation tension
variables.description: Level of adversarial diplomatic rhetoric, formal political measures and perceived bilateral tension raising conflict risk.

catalysts.title: U.S. ramps unprecedented economic pressure on Iran
catalysts.description: Washington is preparing and signalling new, aggressive economic measures aimed at squeezing Iran's finances and trade over coming weeks-to-months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. to use economic tactics on Iran that have never been seen'; 'Trump wants more economic pressure on Iran.'

catalysts.title: Sustained U.S. blockade operations in/around Hormuz
catalysts.description: U.S. statements and naval movements point to a continued, high-pressure maritime interdiction campaign that could be maintained for months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US says it can keep naval blockade on Iran "indefinitely"'; 'Hormuz traffic slows further.'

catalysts.title: Aircraft carrier rotations and fresh deployments
catalysts.description: Pentagon rotations and fresh carrier dispatches to the Middle East will raise concentrated naval assets and operational tempo in the area.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Sending Fresh Aircraft Carrier to Middle East'; 'Pentagon Rotates Aircraft Carriers.'

catalysts.title: Ceasefire/peace-deal deadline and risk of Iranian escalation
catalysts.description: With ceasefire talks stalling and Iran warning it will escalate if a deal isn't honoured within weeks, a near-term escalation risk around the expiry exists.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran says it will escalate if US does not honour deal within weeks'; 'U.S. Futures Mostly Higher as Iran Ceasefire Set to Expire.'

catalysts.title: Continuing attacks on tankers and commercial vessels in Hormuz
catalysts.description: Recent strikes on ADNOC and other vessels indicate an elevated and likely persistent campaign targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'UAE's ADNOC says one of its vessels came under attack'; 'UAE says Iran attacked ADNOC vessel.'

catalysts.title: Oil slicks/off-Oman spill prompting navigation limits
catalysts.description: Two slicks and a large spill off Oman risk continued cleanup and localized navigation restrictions that will affect regional shipping flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Two slicks appear in Gulf as huge oil spill off Oman threatens disaster.'

catalysts.title: Energy Secretary meets refiners to boost fuel output
catalysts.description: U.S. Energy Secretary's meetings with refiners aim to accelerate refinery output or regulatory relief to blunt fuel-price pressure.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Energy Secretary Wright to meet refiners on boosting fuel output.'

catalysts.title: Strategic reserves near damaging low levels
catalysts.description: U.S. strategic oil reserves are approaching levels that risk cavern damage and operational constraints, reducing usable mitigation capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Depleted strategic oil reserve nears level that raises concerns about damage to caverns, operations.'

catalysts.title: Chinese refiners' purchases of sanctioned Iranian oil continue
catalysts.description: Accusations that Chinese refiners are buying sanctioned Iranian oil suggest persistent Iranian export channels that could blunt supply shocks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Chinese refiner Hengli accused of funding Iran through sanctioned oil purchases'; 'This Sprawling Chinese Refinery Is Bankrolling Tehran.'

catalysts.title: Public threats to bomb Oman and potential regional backlash
catalysts.description: Repeated U.S. threats toward Oman raise diplomatic fallout risk and could provoke Gulf-state responses and shifts in regional alignments.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of US-Iran negotiations.'
